nodes.name: Restricted Isometry Property (RIP)
nodes.statement: A linear operator $\calA: \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times d_2}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$ satisfies RIP iff $\forall W$ with $\mathrm{rank}(W)\leq k$: $(1-\delta_k)\|W\|_F^2\leq \|\calA(W)\|_F^2 \leq (1+\delta_k)\|W\|_F^2$, where $\delta_k>0$ depends only on $k$.
nodes.statement_clean: A linear measurement operator is RIP if it preserves Frobenius norms of low-rank matrices up to a constant.

nodes.name: $\mu$-incoherent matrix
nodes.statement: $X\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times n}$ ($d<n$) is $\mu$-incoherent if $\|U_X^i\|_2\leq \frac{\mu\sqrt{d}}{\sqrt{n}}$ for $1\leq i\leq d$, where $X^T=U_X\Sigma_X V_X^T$ is the SVD of $X^T$ and $U_X^i$ is the $i$-th row of $U_X$.
nodes.statement_clean: An incoherence condition bounding row norms of the left singular vectors of $X^T$.

nodes.name: Principal angle subspace distance
nodes.statement: For $k$-dimensional subspaces $U_1, U_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times k}$, $\dist(U_1,U_2)=\|U_\perp^T U_2\|_2$, where $U_\perp$ is an orthonormal basis of the subspace orthogonal to $U_1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Subspace distance via the principal-angle norm of the orthogonal-complement projection.

nodes.name: Low-Rank Matrix Estimation using Rank-One Measurements (LRROM)
nodes.statement: Recover rank-$k$ matrix $\Wo \in \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times d_2}$ from rank-$1$ measurements $b_i=\x_i^T \Wo \y_i$ by solving $\min_{W=UV^T,\, U\in \R^{d_1\times k},\, V\in \R^{d_2\times k}} \sum_{i=1}^m (b_i -\x_i^T W \y_i)^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recover a low-rank matrix from rank-one bilinear measurements via non-convex factored least squares.

nodes.name: Inductive Matrix Completion
nodes.statement: Given user features $X\in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times d_1}$, movie features $Y\in \mathbb{R}^{n_2\times d_2}$, and ratings $R_{ij}=\x_i^T \Wo \y_j$ on a sampled set $\Omega$, recover the rank-$k$ parameter matrix $\Wo \in \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times d_2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recover the low-rank parameter matrix linking user/movie feature vectors to observed ratings.

nodes.name: Rank-One Gaussian Matrix Sensing
nodes.statement: Given $A_i=\x_i\y_i^T$ with $\x_i \sim \calN(0,I)$, $\y_i\sim \calN(0,I)$, and measurements $b_i=\Tr(A_i^T \Wo)$, recover the rank-$k$ matrix $\Wo$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recover a low-rank signal from Gaussian rank-one bilinear sensing measurements.

nodes.name: Multi-label Regression with Missing Labels
nodes.statement: Given training features $X\in \R^{d_1\times n_1}$ and partial label observations $R_{ij}=\e_i^T X^T \Wo \e_j$ on $(i,j)\in \Omega \subseteq [n_1]\times [L]$, recover the low-rank parameter $\Wo \in \R^{d_1\times L}$ such that $X^T \Wo = R$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recover the low-rank regression parameter when many label entries are missing uniformly at random.

nodes.name: Optimal sample complexity for inductive matrix completion
nodes.statement: Reduce sample complexity of inductive matrix completion from $O(k d_1 d_2 \log(d_1 d_2))$ to the information-theoretic optimum $O(k(d_1+d_2)\log(d_1+d_2))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Closing the quadratic-vs-linear gap in feature dimensions for inductive matrix completion.

nodes.name: AltMin-LRROM (Alternating Minimization for LRROM)
nodes.statement: Initialize $U_0$ via top-$k$ SVD of $\frac{1}{m}\sum_i b_i^0 A_i^0$, then alternate least-squares updates of $\widehat{V}_{h+1}$ and $\widehat{U}_{h+1}$ on fresh measurement partitions, orthonormalizing via QR after each step, for $H$ iterations.
nodes.pseudocode: 1. Partition $(\calA_{all},\b_{all})$ into $2H+1$ sets of size $m$. 2. $U_0 \leftarrow$ top-$k$ left singular vectors of $\frac{1}{m}\sum_i b_i^0 A_i^0$. 3. For $h=0,\dots,H-1$: (a) $\widehat{V}_{h+1}\leftarrow \arg\min_V \sum_i (b_i^{2h+1}-\x_i^T U_h V^T \y_i)^2$; $V_{h+1}\leftarrow QR(\widehat{V}_{h+1})$. (b) $\widehat{U}_{h+1}\leftarrow \arg\min_U \sum_i (b_i^{2h+2}-\x_i^T U V_{h+1}^T \y_i)^2$; $U_{h+1}\leftarrow QR(\widehat{U}_{h+1})$. 4. Return $W_H = U_H \widehat{V}_H^T$.

nodes.name: Partition measurements
nodes.statement: Divide $(\calA_{all},\b_{all})$ into $2H+1$ sets of size $m$ to ensure independence of fresh samples from previous iterates.

nodes.name: Spectral initialization of $U_0$
nodes.statement: $U_0 \leftarrow$ top-$k$ left singular vectors of $S = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m b_i^0 A_i^0$.

nodes.name: Alternating least-squares loop
nodes.statement: For $h=0,\dots,H-1$: solve $\widehat{V}_{h+1}=\arg\min_V \sum_i (b_i-\x_i^T U_h V^T \y_i)^2$, orthonormalize via $V_{h+1}=QR(\widehat{V}_{h+1})$; then solve $\widehat{U}_{h+1}=\arg\min_U \sum_i (b_i-\x_i^T U V_{h+1}^T \y_i)^2$ on a fresh partition and set $U_{h+1}=QR(\widehat{U}_{h+1})$.

nodes.name: Return final estimate
nodes.statement: Output $W_H = U_H \widehat{V}_H^T$.

nodes.name: Convergence of AltMin-LRROM under three properties
nodes.statement: If $\calA=\{\x_i\y_i^T\}$ satisfies (1) initialization $\|\frac{1}{m}\sum_i b_i A_i - \Wo\|_2 \le \delta\|\Wo\|_2$, (2) concentration of $B_x,B_y$, and (3) concentration of $G_x,G_y$ with $\delta=\frac{1}{100 k^{3/2}\beta}$, then after $H\le 100\log(\|\Wo\|_F/\epsilon)$ iterations, AltMin-LRROM returns $W_H$ with $\|W_H-\Wo\|_2 \le \epsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under three concentration-type properties of the rank-one measurement operator, alternating minimization converges linearly to $\Wo$.
assumptions: $\Wo \in \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times d_2}$ is rank-$k$ with singular values $\so^1\ge \so^2\ge \dots\ge \so^k$, $\beta=\so^1/\so^k$
Property 3: $\|G_x\|_2 \le \delta$ and $\|G_y\|_2 \le \delta$ for orthogonal unit vectors independent of $\x_i,\y_i$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (rank-1 case + reduction to rank-$k$)
nodes.statement: Prove the rank-$1$ case via gradient-zero analysis of $\widehat{\v}_{h+1}$, bound the perturbation using Properties 2--3, then extend to general rank-$k$ via principal-angle subspace distance and block-matrix identities (Appendix A).

nodes.name: Update equation for $\hvtn$ (rank-1 case)
nodes.statement: Setting the gradient of \eqref{eq:r1ms} w.r.t. $\vh$ to zero with $\ut$ fixed yields $\hvtn = \so(\uot \ut)\vo - \so B^{-1}((\uot\ut)B - \Bo)\vo$, where $B = \frac{1}{m}\sum_i (\x_i^T\ut \ut^T \x_i)\y_i\y_i^T$ and $\Bo = \frac{1}{m}\sum_i (\x_i^T\ut \uo^T\x_i)\y_i\y_i^T$.

nodes.name: Bound perturbation $\|G\|_2$
nodes.statement: Apply Property 2 to obtain $\|B^{-1}\|_2 \le 1/(1-1/100)$ and Property 3 to bound $\|(\uot\ut)B - \Bo\|_2 \le \frac{1}{100}\sqrt{1-(\ut^T\uo)^2}$, yielding $\|G\|_2 \le \frac{1}{99}\sqrt{1-(\ut^T\uo)^2}$.

nodes.name: Lower bound parallel and perpendicular components
nodes.statement: Multiply the update by $\vo$ and $\vo^\perp$ to derive $\vo^T \hvtn \ge \so(\ut^T\uo) - \frac{\so}{99}\sqrt{1-(\ut^T\uo)^2}$ and $\langle \vo^\perp, \hvtn\rangle \le \frac{\so}{99}\sqrt{1-(\ut^T\uo)^2}$.

nodes.name: Initialization quality $\u_0^T\uo \ge 9/10$
nodes.statement: From Property 1, $\|S\|_2 \ge \frac{99 \so}{100}$ and $\|S\|_2 - \so \v_0^T\vo \u_0^T\uo \le \so/100$, hence $\u_0^T\uo \ge 9/10$.

nodes.name: Geometric error decay (induction on $h$)
nodes.statement: Combining the above with the inductive hypothesis $\u_h^T\uo \ge 9/10$ gives $1-(\v_{h+1}^T \vo)^2 \le \frac{1}{2}(1-(\ut^T\uo)^2)$ and symmetrically for $\u$, yielding linear convergence after $H = O(\log(\so/\epsilon))$ steps.

nodes.name: Generalize to rank-$k$ via block matrices
nodes.statement: Setting the gradient w.r.t. $\Vh$ to zero gives $\Vh = \Wo^T U - F$ with $\mathrm{vec}(F) = B^{-1}(BD-C)S\,\mathrm{vec}(\Vo)$, where $B,C,D,S \in \R^{kd_2\times kd_2}$ are block matrices defined by Eqs.~(\ref{eq:Bpq})--(\ref{eq:Spq}).

nodes.name: Subspace distance recursion
nodes.statement: Using $V = \Vh R^{-1}$ and projecting onto $\Vop$ yields $\dist(\Vo, V_{t+1}) \le \|F\|_2 \|R^{-1}\|_2$; combined with Lemmas $\|F\|_2$ and $\|R^{-1}\|_2$ this gives the rank-$k$ convergence rate.

nodes.name: $\calA_{Gauss}$ does not satisfy RIP for $m=O((d_1+d_2)\log^c(d_1+d_2))$
nodes.statement: If $\x_i \sim \calN(0,I)$, $\y_i \sim \calN(0,I)$, and $m=O((d_1+d_2)\log^c(d_1+d_2))$ for any constant $c>0$, then with probability $\ge 1-1/m^{10}$, $\calA_{Gauss}$ does NOT satisfy RIP for rank-$1$ matrices with constant $\delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Rank-one Gaussian operators fail RIP at near-linear sample complexity.
conclusions: With probability $\ge 1 - 1/m^{10}$, $\calA_{Gauss}$ does not satisfy RIP for rank-$1$ matrices with a constant $\delta$

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1 (non-RIP via $Z_U,Z_L$ separation)
nodes.statement: Construct $Z_U=\x_1\y_1^T$ and $Z_L=\u\v^T$ with $\u,\v$ independent of $X,Y$; show $\|\calA_{Gauss}(Z_U)\|^2 \ge 0.5 d_1^2 d_2^2$ while $\|\calA_{Gauss}(Z_L)\|^2 \le 4m d_1 d_2 \log^4 m$, forcing the RIP gap unless $m=\Omega(d_1 d_2/\log)$.

nodes.name: Lower bound for $\|\calA_{Gauss}(Z_U)\|_2^2$
nodes.statement: With $Z_U = \x_1 \y_1^T$, the dominant term gives $\|\x_1\|^4 \|\y_1\|^4 \ge 0.5 d_1^2 d_2^2$ w.p. $\ge 1-2\exp(-d_1-d_2)$, hence $\|\calA_{Gauss}(Z_U)\|_2^2 \ge 0.5 d_1^2 d_2^2$.

nodes.name: Upper bound for $\|\calA_{Gauss}(Z_L)\|_2^2$
nodes.statement: With $Z_L=\u\v^T$ (independent), $|\u^T\x_i| \le \log m \|\u\|_2$ and $|\v^T\y_i|\le \log m\|\v\|_2$ w.h.p., giving $\|\calA_{Gauss}(Z_L)\|_2^2 \le 4m d_1 d_2 \log^4 m$.

nodes.name: RIP gap forces $m = \Omega(d_1 d_2/\log)$
nodes.statement: Combining the two bounds: $40 m \log^4 m \le \|\calA_{Gauss}(Z/\|Z\|_F)\|^2 \le 0.05 d_1 d_2$. Constant-ratio RIP requires $m = \Omega(d_1 d_2 / \log(5 d_1 d_2))$.

nodes.name: Rank-One Gaussian Measurements satisfy Properties 1--3
nodes.statement: If $\x_i \in \R^{d_1}\sim \calN(0,I)$, $\y_i\in \R^{d_2}\sim \calN(0,I)$ and $m=\Omega(k^4 \beta^2 (d_1+d_2)\log^3(d_1+d_2))$, then Properties 1, 2, 3 of Theorem~\ref{thm:general} are satisfied with probability $\ge 1 - 1/(d_1+d_2)^{100}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gaussian rank-one operators satisfy the three concentration properties at near-linear sample size.
conclusions: Properties 1, 2, 3 of Theorem 1 hold with probability $\ge 1-1/(d_1+d_2)^{100}$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (Property 1 via clipped matrix Bernstein)
nodes.statement: Apply Tropp's matrix Bernstein bound to clipped variables $\wt{Z}_i$, control $\|\wt{Z}_i\|_2$ and second-moment terms, then transfer back to unclipped variables via union bound.

nodes.name: Decompose $S$ as sum of $Z_i$
nodes.statement: $S = \frac{1}{m}\sum_i \x_i \x_i^T \Uo \So \Vo^T \y_i \y_i^T = \frac{1}{m}\sum_i Z_i$ with $\E[Z_i]=\Wo$; by rotational invariance assume $\Uo, \Vo$ have canonical-basis columns.

nodes.name: Clip Gaussian coordinates
nodes.statement: Define $\wt{x}_{ij}=x_{ij}\,\mathbf{1}[|x_{ij}|\le C\sqrt{\log(m(d_1+d_2))}]$ and similarly $\wt{y}_{ij}$; show $\Pr(x_{ij}=\wt{x}_{ij})\ge 1 - 1/(m(d_1+d_2))^C$ and $\E[\wt{x}_{ij}^2]\ge 1 - O(\log m / m^{C^2/2})$.

nodes.name: Apply Tropp matrix Bernstein and transfer to $Z_i$
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{thm:tropp}, $\|\frac{1}{m}\sum_i \wt{Z}_i - \E[\wt{Z}_i]\|_2 \le \delta$ w.p. $\ge 1 - (d_1+d_2)^{-10}$. Union-bounding over the clipping events gives $\|\frac{1}{m}\sum_i Z_i - \Wo\|_2 \le 5\delta\|\Wo\|_2$, and choosing $\delta = 1/(100 k^{3/2}\beta)$ proves Property 1.

nodes.name: Inductive Matrix Completion satisfies Properties 1--3
nodes.statement: If $X\in \R^{d_1\times n_1}$ and $Y\in \R^{d_2\times n_2}$ are $\mu$-incoherent, $R = X^T \Wo Y$, and $\Omega \subseteq [n_1]\times [n_2]$ is a uniform random subset with $|\Omega|=m \ge C k^3 \beta^2 d_1 d_2 \log(d_1+d_2)$, then with probability $\ge 1-1/(d_1+d_2)^{100}$, the operators $A_{ij}=\sqrt{n_1 n_2}\, \x_i \y_j^T$ satisfy Properties 1--3 of Theorem 1.
nodes.statement_clean: Incoherent feature matrices and a uniformly random sampling mask yield the three concentration properties at $\tilde O(d_1 d_2)$ samples.
assumptions: $\Wo$ is a fixed rank-$k$ matrix with condition number $\beta = \sigma_R^1/\sigma_R^k$
$\Omega$ uniformly random in $[n_1]\times [n_2]$ with $|\Omega|=m \ge C k^3 \beta^2 d_1 d_2 \log(d_1+d_2)$
conclusions: Properties 1, 2, 3 of Theorem 1 hold for $A_{ij}=\sqrt{n_1 n_2}\,\x_i \y_j^T$ w.p. $\ge 1-1/(d_1+d_2)^{100}$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2 (orthonormalization + Tropp on each property)
nodes.statement: WLOG assume $X,Y$ orthonormal (transformation preserves condition number); for each property, bound $\max\|Z_{ij}\|_2$ and the matrix variance using incoherence, then apply Theorem~\ref{thm:tropp}.

nodes.name: Reduce to orthonormal $X,Y$
nodes.statement: Write $R = X^T \Wo Y = U_X (\Sigma_X V_X^T \Wo V_Y \Sigma_Y) U_Y^T$ and absorb $\Sigma_X V_X^T$ and $V_Y \Sigma_Y$ into a redefined $\Wo$; the new $\Wo$ has the same condition number as $R$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|Z_{ij}\|_2$ and matrix variance via incoherence (Property 1)
nodes.statement: Show $\|Z_{ij}\|_2 \le \so^1\mu^4 d_1 d_2 / (n_1 n_2)$ and $\|\sum_{(i,j)\in \Omega}\E[Z_{ij}Z_{ij}^T]\|_2 \le (\so^1)^2 \mu^4 d_1 d_2 / (n_1^2 n_2^2)\cdot m$ via the incoherence of $X,Y$.

nodes.name: Apply Tropp to obtain Property 1
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{thm:tropp} and the bounds above, $\|S-\Wo\|_2 \le \so^1 \mu^2 \sqrt{d_1 d_2 \log(2(d_1+d_2)/\gamma)/m}$, so $m=\Omega(\mu^4 k^3 \beta^2 d_1 d_2 \log)$ delivers $\|S-\Wo\|_2 \le \delta\|\Wo\|_2$.

nodes.name: Properties 2 and 3 by analogous Tropp arguments
nodes.statement: Define $B_y = \frac{n_1 n_2}{m}\sum Z_{ij}$ with $Z_{ij}=\x_i^T \u \u^T \x_i \y_i \y_i^T$, bound $\|Z_{ij}\|_2 \le \mu^4 d_1 d_2/(n_1 n_2)$ and the matrix variance, then Tropp gives $\|B_y-I\|_2\le\delta$. Property 3 ($\|C_y\|_2 \le \delta$) follows analogously.

nodes.name: Multi-label Regression with Missing Labels satisfies Properties 1--3
nodes.statement: If $X\in \R^{d_1\times n_1}$ is $\mu$-incoherent, $R = X^T\Wo$, and $\Omega \subseteq [n_1]\times [L]$ is uniformly random with $|\Omega|=m \ge C \beta^2 d_1 n_2 \log(d_1+n_2)$, then with probability $\ge 1-1/(d_1+L)^{100}$ the operators $A_{ij}=\sqrt{n_1 n_2}\,\x_i \e_j^T$ satisfy Properties 1--3 of Theorem 1.
nodes.statement_clean: For incoherent feature matrices and random label sampling, the multi-label rank-one operator satisfies the three concentration properties.
assumptions: $\Omega$ uniformly random in $[n_1]\times [L]$ with $|\Omega|=m\ge C \beta^2 d_1 n_2 \log(d_1+n_2)$
conclusions: Properties 1, 2, 3 hold for $A_{ij}=\sqrt{n_1 n_2}\,\x_i \e_j^T$ with probability $\ge 1-1/(d_1+L)^{100}$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3 (mixed inductive/canonical measurement Tropp argument)
nodes.statement: Adapt the proof of Lemma 2 to mixed measurement vectors $\x_i, \e_j$: bound $\|Z_{ij}\|_2 \le \so^1 \mu^2 d_1/n_1$ and the matrix variance using only $X$-incoherence, then apply Tropp to get all three properties at $m = \tilde\Omega(d_1 L)$.

nodes.name: Spectral and variance bounds (Property 1)
nodes.statement: Show $\|Z_{ij}\|_2 \le \so^1 \mu^2 d_1/n_1$ and $\|\sum_{(i,j)}\E[Z_{ij}Z_{ij}^T]\|_2, \|\sum_{(i,j)}\E[Z_{ij}^TZ_{ij}]\|_2 \le (\so^1)^2\mu^2 d_1 m/(n_1^2 n_2)$ via incoherence of $X$ and uniform sampling of $\e_j$.

nodes.name: Apply Tropp to derive Property 1
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:tropp} with the bounds yields $\Pr(\|S-\Wo\|_2 \ge n_2 \so^1\gamma/(\mu\sqrt{k})) \le 2(d_1+n_2)\exp(-m\gamma^2/(\mu^4 k d_1(1+\gamma/3)))$; choose $m=\Omega(k^3\beta^2 \mu^2 d_1 n_2 \log)$ to get $\|S-\Wo\|_2 \le \delta\|\Wo\|_2$.

nodes.name: Properties 2 and 3 via analogous Tropp arguments
nodes.statement: For $B_y$ and $B_x$ with mixed $\x_i, \e_j$, bound $\|Z_{ij}\|_2 \le \mu^2 d_1/n_1$ and matrix variance $\le \mu^2 d_1/(n_1^2 n_2)$; Tropp gives $\|B_y-I\|_2,\|B_x-I\|_2,\|C_x\|_2,\|C_y\|_2 \le \delta$ at the same sample size.

nodes.name: Bound on $\|F\|_2$ (rank-$k$ error matrix)
nodes.statement: If $\calA$ satisfies Properties 1--3 of Theorem 1 and $\Wo$ has singular values $\so^1 \ge \dots \ge \so^k$, then $\|F\|_2 \le \frac{\so^k}{100}\dist(U_t,\Uo)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Spectral bound on the error matrix in the rank-$k$ alternating-minimization update.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma F-bound (block matrix singular-value analysis)
nodes.statement: Show $\sigma_{\min}(B)\ge 1-k\delta$ via block decomposition and Properties 2--3, bound $\|BD-C\|_2 \le k\delta\dist(U,\Uo)$ via Property 3, then combine with $\|F\|_2 \le \so^1\sqrt{k}\|B^{-1}\|_2\|BD-C\|_2$ and $\delta=1/(100 k^{3/2}\beta)$.

nodes.name: Bound on $\|R^{-1}\|_2$ (QR factor of $\widehat{V}$)
nodes.statement: If $\calA$ satisfies Properties 1--3 of Theorem 1, then $\|R^{-1}\|_2 \le \frac{1}{\so^k\sqrt{1-\dist^2(U_t,\Uo)} - \|F\|_2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Inverse spectral bound on the QR factor controlling $V_{t+1}$ via subspace distance and the error norm.

nodes.name: Proof of $R^{-1}$ bound (reproduced from JainNS13)
nodes.statement: Bound $\sigma_{\min}(R)$ from below using $\|VR\z\|_2 \ge \|\Vo\So\Uo^T U\z\|_2 - \|F\z\|_2$ and the sin-theta identity $\sigma_{\min}(U^T\Uo) \ge \sqrt{1-\dist(U,\Uo)^2}$.

nodes.name: Tropp matrix Bernstein inequality
nodes.statement: For independent random matrices $Z_i \in \R^{d_1\times d_2}$ with $\E[Z_i]=0$ and $\|Z_i\|_2 \le R$ a.s., letting $\sigma^2 = \max\{\|\sum_i \E[Z_i Z_i^T]\|_2, \|\sum_i \E[Z_i^T Z_i]\|_2\}$, $\Pr(\|\frac{1}{m}\sum_i Z_i\|_2 \ge \gamma) \le (d_1+d_2)\exp(-m^2\gamma^2/(\sigma^2 + Rm\gamma/3))$.
nodes.statement_clean: A matrix Bernstein-type tail bound for sums of independent bounded zero-mean random matrices.

nodes.name: Sin-theta theorem for singular vector perturbation
nodes.statement: If $\|S - \Wo\|_2 \le \so^k/100$, then for $U_0$ formed from the top-$k$ left singular vectors of $S$, $\dist(U_0, \Uo) \le 1/100$.
nodes.statement_clean: Spectral perturbation of subspaces under matrix perturbation (Wedin/Davis-Kahan).

nodes.name: AltMin convergence under RIP (prior work)
nodes.statement: Under standard assumptions including RIP, alternating minimization for low-rank matrix sensing and matrix completion converges at a linear rate to the global optimum.
nodes.statement_clean: Cited prior result establishing global optimality of alternating minimization under RIP.

nodes.name: Linear measurement operator
nodes.statement: $\calA(W) = [\Tr(A_1^T W)\ \Tr(A_2^T W)\ \dots\ \Tr(A_m^T W)]^T$.

nodes.name: LRROM non-convex factored objective
nodes.statement: $\min_{W=UV^T,\, U\in \R^{d_1\times k},\, V\in \R^{d_2\times k}}\, \sum_{i=1}^m (b_i - \x_i^T W \y_i)^2$.

nodes.name: Rank-1 perturbation update for $\hvtn$
nodes.statement: $\hvtn = \so(\uo^T\ut)\vo - \so B^{-1}((\uo^T\ut)B - \Bo)\vo$.

nodes.name: Rank-$k$ error matrix factorization
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{vec}(F) = B^{-1}(BD - C) S \cdot \mathrm{vec}(\Vo)$.

nodes.name: Synthetic rank-5 matrix sensing experiment
nodes.statement: Generate random rank-$5$ $\Wo \in \R^{50\times 50}$, compare $\calA_{Gauss}$ vs RIP-based measurement operator on AltMin: rank-one operator achieves similar Frobenius recovery error at $\approx$ two orders of magnitude lower runtime.

nodes.name: Multi-label regression on synthetic data
nodes.statement: With $L=50$ labels, $n_1=100$ training points, $d$ varying $1$--$20$, observing $200$ random entries of $R = X^T \Wo$, AltMin produces accurate test predictions and degrades gracefully as $k$ or $d$ grows.

nodes.name: Sample partitioning enables independence
nodes.statement: Partitioning $\calA_{all}$ into $2H+1$ disjoint sets ensures intermediate vectors $\u, \v, \u_\perp, \v_\perp$ are independent of the measurements at each step, costing a $\log(\|\Wo\|_F/\epsilon)$ blow-up in total samples.

nodes.name: Universality vs randomness tradeoff
nodes.statement: RIP operators are universal but expensive; $\calA_{Gauss}$ must be resampled per signal $\Wo$ but is dramatically more efficient. Intermediate operators trading randomness for universality may exist.
